thought: Root cause confirmed. In pyshop/inventory.py:20, `Inventory.reserve` guards with a strict `self.available(sku) > qty`. When qty equals available (reserve 3 of 3), `3 > 3` is False, so control falls to the else branch at line 23 and raises OutOfStock. The docstring (line 17) and README rule ('Reserving exactly the remaining stock is allowed') both state equality must be permitted, and test_reserve_too_many_raises confirms that over-requesting must still raise. The fix belongs in the condition operator (`>` should be `>=`); the crash site (line 23) is just the symptom. No other method is implicated: available() (line 14) correctly computes stock minus reserved, and the rest of the file is consistent.

When a customer requests exactly the remaining stock (e.g., reserve("A", 3) with available("A") == 3), `3 > 3` evaluates False, so execution falls into the else branch and raises OutOfStock at line 23. This contradicts the method docstring ('Reserving exactly the remaining quantity is allowed', line 17) and the documented domain rule, so the last units of any product can never be reserved.

payload.rationale: The root cause is the strict comparison in Inventory.reserve: `if self.available(sku) > qty:` requires strictly more stock than requested, so reserving exactly the remaining quantity (qty == available) falls into the else branch and raises OutOfStock. Changing `>` to `>=` allows a reservation equal to the available stock (per the docstring and README domain rule), while still raising OutOfStock when qty exceeds available — preserving the behavior required by test_reserve_too_many_raises. This is the smallest possible change: one operator on one line.
